clue.text: To fish or not to fish? This could decide

definitions.text: To fish or not to fish? This could decide

parts.words: To fish or not to fish? This could decide
parts.note: fishing with a rod and line is ..., so the deciding ballot in a tied meeting is read as a fisherman's choice

explanation.surface: An angler dithers over whether to go fishing and looks for something to settle it.
explanation.walkthrough: A chairman's deciding ballot breaks a tie; the pun is that casting is also what an angler does with a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair's extra ballot that settles a tied division is what decides the question.

clue.text: Leapt about in a saucy way!

definitions.meaning: to caper is to skip or frolic, so this is the past tense of jumping playfully
jokingly, served with caper sauce, the pickled flower buds used in cooking

explanation.surface: Someone jumped around cheekily.
explanation.definitionFit: Frolicking is skipping around; the joke second sense is a dish dressed with a sauce of pickled buds.

clue.text: Joint where Elia's tearful wife found comfort?

definitions.text: Joint where Elia's tearful wife found comfort?

parts.words: Joint where Elia's tearful wife found comfort?
parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb, so a weeping wife would cry on that writer's shoulder; the joint is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Asks where an essayist's weeping wife was consoled.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia is the pen name of Charles Lamb, the English essayist; crying on someone's shoulder is being comforted by them.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting joint cut from the upper foreleg of a young sheep.

clue.text: Locals in Nova Scotia

parts.note: NS is the standard abbreviation for the Canadian province of Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood residents of a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' looks like people, but in Britain your local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a local is a neighbourhood pub, and pubs were once called taverns or hostelries.

clue.text: Game fellow on leave in a naval area

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits below it, so the fellow comes after the departure

parts.note: to leave is to go
a sport is a good-natured person who is game for anything

explanation.surface: A plucky man on shore leave in a port district.
explanation.walkthrough: GOSPORT is a Hampshire town on Portsmouth Harbour, long home to Royal Navy establishments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire harbour town has been a Royal Navy base for centuries.

clue.text: See 1
Cover living rough around the English capital

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the capital letter so as to enclose it
done roughly, the letters of living are knocked about into a new order
the capital of a word is its opening letter, here the head of English

explanation.surface: A shelter for people sleeping rough in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns LIVING into VILING, and 'around' puts that round E, the first letter (capital) of English.
explanation.definitionFit: Veiling is a covering, a fabric draped to conceal.

clue.text: Gin could be a hidden danger

definitions.meaning: a gin is a snare for catching animals
a pitfall or concealed hazard laid to catch someone

explanation.surface: A warning that the spirit might be a concealed threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for game; figuratively the same word covers any pitfall waiting for the unwary.

clue.text: Singer with a place in a Lisbon beauty spot

indicators.note: the instruction to place the letter inside means it goes within the town's name

parts.note: Sintra is a famously scenic hill town near Lisbon in Portugal

explanation.surface: A vocalist owns a property in a picturesque Portuguese town.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Sinatra was the American crooner; Sintra is a palace-studded town just outside Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American crooner.

clue.text: Notice sent round may mean nothing

definitions.meaning: a notice copied and distributed to many recipients
the round character O stands for zero

explanation.surface: A distributed notice might turn out to say nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: the letter O is circular and also represents zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice duplicated for wide distribution; the cryptic sense is the round letter O, which also means zero.

clue.text: Anyhow, one can't go to prison for such a forecast

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A prediction that no one will be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' scrambles I (one) with CANTGOTOPRISON; the apostrophe is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognostication is a prediction of what will happen.

clue.text: Thrilling little flower with nothing

indicators.note: read as with no thing: the word thing is removed letter by letter from the clue word before it

explanation.surface: An exciting small bloom with nothing else to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T, H, I, N, G (with 'no thing') from THRILLING leaves RILL. A 'flower' in crosswords is often a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small stream, and a stream is something that flows.

clue.text: Company Mick endlessly finds amusing

indicators.note: without its end, the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A firm's employee called Mick finds something funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny, causing laughter.

clue.text: Payment on land north of the Tweed

definitions.meaning: ... is an old word for a tax or levy, as in ...-free

definitions.text: on land north of the Tweed
definitions.meaning: someone from the country beyond the River Tweed, the Anglo-Scottish border

explanation.surface: Money handed over in the Scottish borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Tweed forms part of the border between England and Scotland; scot-free originally meant untaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tax or levy, surviving in scot-free; also a native of the country beyond the Tweed border.

clue.text: Colour intrinsically Latin given space

definitions.meaning: a dark greyish-blue shade
the Latin phrase ... means intrinsically, and splitting the word with a space produces it

explanation.surface: A shade that is essentially Latin and needs room.
explanation.definitionFit: Perse is a dark blue-grey shade; with a space inserted it is the Latin tag for in itself.

clue.text: A river in dotage

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A waterway grown old and doddery.
explanation.definitionFit: Anile means like a feeble old woman, senile.

clue.text: Lowest form of annoyance on the river

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
a pest is a nuisance, an annoying thing

explanation.surface: The worst kind of nuisance by the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest point is the lowest one.

clue.text: Nerve-centres giving a body of workers back trouble

parts.note: a gang is a group of labourers

indicators.note: back means the word for trouble is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A workforce that gives a team back pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganglia are clusters of nerve cells acting as relay centres.

clue.text: Calls to urge reform on an evildoer?

definitions.meaning: pays a casual visit

definitions.text: to urge reform on an evildoer?
definitions.meaning: read as an instruction to give up wrongdoing: abandon wickedness

explanation.surface: Appeals for a wrongdoer to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Visits casually; split, the words tell a sinner to give up wrongdoing.

clue.text: Collapse of apple-pie bed Alec made

indicators.note: a bed that is made is put in order, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An apple-pie bed, a prank where sheets are folded so you cannot stretch out, made by Alec falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a British schoolboy prank with the sheet folded back; 'of apple-pie' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden collapse or fiasco.

clue.text: Denied being shut in on Tyneside

indicators.note: in a down clue the confinement word sits on the region abbreviation, so it comes after it

parts.note: Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE
gated means confined to college or home as a punishment

explanation.surface: Refused when locked up in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is British slang for grounded, confined indoors as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Negated means nullified or refused.

clue.text: Vital point when it comes to the purchase

definitions.text: Vital point when it comes to the purchase

parts.words: Vital point when it comes to the purchase
parts.note: purchase here means mechanical grip or leverage, and the pivot of a lever is what gives it

explanation.surface: Sounds like the key consideration when buying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like shopping but means leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The pivot of a lever is the point on which leverage depends.

clue.text: Gets rid of one with a plant

parts.note: frees means releases or clears away
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone disposes of one gardening item.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa.

clue.text: Harmonises in striking fashion

definitions.meaning: goes well with, suits
small sticks lit by striking

explanation.surface: Coordinates outfits in eye-catching style.
explanation.definitionFit: Goes together; also the sticks one strikes to light a flame.

clue.text: Fitting for a nut to make a get away

definitions.meaning: a threaded metal pin onto which a nut is screwed
to run off suddenly

explanation.surface: A piece of hardware that lets a madman escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded rod paired with a nut; also to dash off suddenly.

clue.text: Looks pleased to see you

parts.note: describes staring at someone with amorous interest

explanation.surface: Someone appears happy to meet you.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone with obvious desire.

clue.text: Novel time for an amphibian

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: A new era for a frog-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tailed amphibian related to the salamander.

clue.text: Meditate with Calliope, say

definitions.meaning: to ponder or reflect
Calliope is one of the nine goddesses of the arts, presiding over epic poetry

explanation.surface: Reflect in the company of a Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder; Calliope is one of the nine Greek goddesses who inspire the arts.

clue.text: Worry over a key pattern in architecture

definitions.meaning: to be anxious
a Greek key ornament of interlocking right-angled lines

explanation.surface: Anxiety about a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anxious; also the Greek key ornamental band in classical design.

clue.text: How the diver irritated at work fulfilled his obligation

definitions.text: How the diver irritated at work fulfilled his obligation

parts.words: How the diver irritated at work fulfilled his obligation
parts.note: a diver rises to the surface, and an itchy one would have a scratch, so surfacing and scratching combine into an idiom for meeting a standard

explanation.surface: Tells of a diver, itching on the job, who did his duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for reaching the required standard, from boxers toeing the line drawn on the ground.

clue.text: Crazy about energy-packed drink

indicators.note: the word for crazy goes about, around, the energy letter

parts.note: mad means crazy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone wild about a high-energy beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey.

clue.text: Busybodies are taken in by this brilliant giant

indicators.note: the second piece is taken in, held inside, by the first

parts.note: ants are proverbially busy creatures

explanation.surface: Nosy people are fooled by a dazzling big figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Antares is the bright red supergiant star in Scorpius.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant star, one of the brightest in the sky.
